issues.legal_issue: The evidence, considered as a whole, sufficiently established the genuineness and voluntary character of a will despite the circumstances treated by the lower courts as suspicious.
material_facts: The testatrix left natural heirs out of the will, although some descendants of one branch of the family were beneficiaries.
The objection did not assert that the lawyer who identified the testatrix before the registrar had identified the wrong person.
The will and two later codicils were registered, and the registrar explained or read their contents to the testatrix.
Some attesting witnesses were interested in the executors.
A close relation of one executor played an active role in arranging execution of the will.
The testatrix made two codicils, the later one about three years after the will, because she had used some of the property listed in it.
The testatrix also sold property and received the price, and executed a fixed deposit receipt, demonstrating that she could deal with her property.
issues.conclusion: The suspicious circumstances relied on by the lower courts did not outweigh the evidence supporting the testatrix’s voluntary and informed execution of the documents. The appeal was allowed, the lower courts’ judgments were set aside, and the will as modified by the two codicils was probated.
issues.legal_principle: A will expresses the testator’s last wishes, but the propounder must remove suspicious circumstances before probate may be granted. Disinheriting natural heirs is not, by itself, suspicious because testamentary disposition departs from the ordinary line of succession. Identification before a registrar is not suspicious where the identity is not disputed. Where a registered will has been read or explained to the testator and its contents admitted, interest on the part of attesting witnesses loses significance. An active role by a person close to an executor may raise concern, but that concern must be assessed against the other evidence. The circumstances must be considered as a whole. The judgment cites no statutory provisions or earlier cases.

rule.if: probate_appeal_from_refusal and registered_documents_explained and later_codicils_reflect_testator_choices and independent_property_dealings and (ordinary_heirs_disinherited or interested_attesting_witnesses or close_relation_arranged_execution)

predicates.probate_appeal_from_refusal: The proceeding was an appeal from a refusal to grant probate of a will.
predicates.registered_documents_explained: The will and related testamentary documents were registered, and an official read or explained their contents to the testator.
predicates.later_codicils_reflect_testator_choices: The testator later made codicils that reflected changes arising from the testator’s use or disposition of property covered by the will.
predicates.independent_property_dealings: The testator independently sold property, received its price, or otherwise dealt with property in a manner showing awareness and capacity.
predicates.ordinary_heirs_disinherited: The testator excluded natural heirs from some or all of the testamentary benefit.
predicates.interested_attesting_witnesses: One or more attesting witnesses had an interest connected with the beneficiaries or executors.
predicates.close_relation_arranged_execution: A person close to an executor took an active role in arranging execution of the testamentary documents.
predicates.will_as_modified_probated: The will, as modified by its codicils, is granted probate.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges refusal of probate and the registered documents were explained, later codicils reflect the testator’s choices, and independent property dealings support capacity, the will as modified is probated even if one or more listed circumstances are present.
